Multiple dodge bonuses (from different [[feat]]s or racial bonuses) are cumulative. |icon=ife_mobility.gif |bonus1=champion of Torm |bonus2=fighter }}
==Notes== * A high [[tumble]] skill reduces the need for this feat, as the tumble skill can prevent attacks of opportunity from moving in combat. However, the usefulness of ''mobility'' is not eliminated since there are other conditions that provoke attacks of opportunity. Furthermore, the [[armor check penalty]] makes achieving a high tumble skill difficult for characters who wear [[heavy armor]] and/or carry a [[tower shield]]. * The AC bonus does not count toward the +20 dodge AC cap.
==Builder notes== '''Item feat:''' yes

'''Reusable:''' yes
'''Script:''' hardcoded

{| class="centertable" style="text-align:center" !Shape!!Str!!Dex!!Con!!Temp HP!!Dodge AC bonus!!Base AC |- |align=left|Rakshasa ||17||20||-||+30||+12||27 |- |align=left|Death slaad ||22||19||18||+70||+16||29 (30 -1 large size) |- |align=left|Azer chief ||20||-||21||+50||+13||- |}
* '''Rakshasa shape:''' Can cast [[ice storm]], [[Mestil's acid breath]] and [[dispel magic]] unlimited times per day. **Like an NPC rakshasa, a shifter is vulnerable to [[blessed bolt|blessed crossbow bolts]] with the ''on-hit: slay rakshasa'' ability. **[[Damage reduction]]: 15/+5 **Immunity to level 8 spells and lower. **Skill bonuses: +15 [[spellcraft]], +11 [[move silently]], +10 [[hide]], +10 [[spot]], +5 [[discipline]] **Bonus feats: [[dodge]], [[knockdown]], [[true seeing]] **Universal save +2 **Merges weapons, items, and armor. **Weapon: ''rakshasa staff +5'', 1d10 [[fire damage]] *'''Death slaad shape:''' Is large-sized (-1 AB, -1 AC, -4 hide). ** It has the [[chaos spittle]] ability, a ranged [[touch attack]] that deals (shifter levels / 3 + 2)d4 [[magical damage]]. **Regeneration +5 **Immunity to [[fear]]. **Damage reduction 10/+5 **[[Damage resistance]]: acid/10, cold/10, electricity/10, fire/10, sonic/10 **Bonus feats: [[cleave]], [[power attack]] **Merges armor only. *'''Azer shape:''' ** Can cast [[burning hands]] and [[fire stream]] unlimited times per day. **Spell resistance 12 **Immunity increased: fire 100% **Immunity decreased: cold 50% **Weapon: ''azer flaming waraxe +5'' (really a [[dwarven waraxe]]) 2d4 fire damage **Bonus feats: [[cleave]], [[knockdown]], [[power attack]] **Merges weapons, items, and armor.
* The spells ''burning hands'', ''ice storm'', ''Mestil's acid breath'', and ''dispel magic'' are the same spells that can be found in a [[spellbook]]. Thus [[quickslot]]s for these spells can be used to cast the (unlimited) shifted abilities, and can be used to apply [[metamagic]]. See [[shifted ability]] for details.
== Custom content notes ==
*A custom class must have this feat in their feat list, or that class will not be able to select it as a general feat.
[[category:feats restricted by class, epic]]

'''Instant feats''' are [[feat]]s that need to be activated to use, but that take effect instantly. Unlike most feats, instant feats bypass the [[action queue]] and lack an activation animation. Instant feats were added in [[patch]] 1.66, but no official content made use of these until patch 1.69, at which point the following instant feats were added to the game: [[rallying cry]], [[heroic shield]], [[oath of wrath]], [[horse menu]] (and all sub-options), [[DM tool]]s, and [[player tool]]s. == Custom content notes == * A feat is specified as being an instant feat if its "ReqAction" column in [[feat.2da]] is 0. [[category:feats| Instant feat]]

{{feat |icon=ife_ptool10.gif |type=instant custom |prereq=none |desc=This instant feat can be given to players to enable a behavior you desire. The feat does nothing unless implemented in a community-made [[module]]. The feat is implemented by editing the x3_pl_tool## [[script]] in the [[Toolset]] and then giving the feat to a [[player character]]. This can be done by adding an [[item property]] bonus feat to a [[skin item|creature skin]] that has been previously equipped on the player character through scripting. |use=selected }} == Notes == * Added in [[patch]] 1.69. * There are ten of these feats — player tool 1 to player tool 10. * These feats appear under the [[base class]] special abilities in the [[radial menu]], which happens to always put them next to the [[horse menu]]. * The intent of these feats is to relieve the reliance upon [[item]]s to give players easy access to certain custom scripts. They also eliminate the activation animation associated with item use. A player can select any of these tools from the radial menu, then select a target (which could be ignored, depending on the implementation), thereby initiating whatever actions the module builder associated with that tool. == Builder notes == '''Item feat:''' yes (intended use) == Custom content notes == '''Removable:''' yes '''Reusable:''' yes (no default behavior) '''Scripts:''' x3_pl_tool01 through x3_pl_tool10

{{feat |icon=ife_dmtool10.gif |type=instant custom |prereq=none |desc=All [[Dungeon Master|DM]] characters start with this instant feat. This feat does nothing unless implemented in a community-made [[module]]. The feat is implemented by editing the x3_dm_tool## [[script]] in the [[Toolset]]. |use=selected }} == Notes == * Added in [[patch]] 1.69. * There are ten of these feats — DM tool 1 to DM tool 10. * The intent of these feats is to relieve the reliance upon [[item]]s to give DMs easy access to certain custom scripts. They also eliminate the activation animation associated with item use. A DM can select any of these tools from the [[radial menu]], then select a target (which could be ignored, depending on the implementation), thereby initiating whatever actions the module builder associated with that tool. == Builder notes == '''Item feat:''' yes, but ineffective Access to these feats is hardcoded into the graphical interface for DMs, and all DMs automatically have these feats. So the only use in putting this feat on an item would be to give ordinary players access to these tools. However, players have no way to activate these tools unless the various [[cls_feat_*.2da]] files are edited. == Custom content notes == '''Removable:''' no (DM interface is hardcoded) '''Reusable:''' yes (no default behavior) '''Scripts:''' x3_dm_tool01 through x3_dm_tool10

(warhammer)]] |[[Image:Ife x2ocrtwhip.gif|right|Overwhelming critical (whip)]] |} {{feat |epic=yes |type=combat |prereq=21st level, [[strength]] 23+, [[cleave]], [[great cleave]], [[improved critical]] (chosen weapon), [[power attack]] |reqfor=[[devastating critical]] |desc=When using the weapon chosen, the character deals +1d6 points of damage on a successful [[critical hit]]. If the weapon's [[critical multiplier]] is x3, add +2d6 and if the multiplier is x4, add 3d6. |use=automatic |bonus1=arcane archer |bonus2=barbarian |bonus3=blackguard |bonus4=champion of Torm |bonus5=dwarven defender |bonus6=fighter |bonus7=paladin |bonus8=weapon master }}
== Notes ==
*Requires [[Hordes of the Underdark]]. *Most NWN manuals state that [[weapon focus]] is a prerequisite, but it is not. * This feat [[stack]]s with any [[massive critical]] item property on a weapon (including that obtained from [[thundering rage]]). * The number of extra dice rolled does not match the feat's description. ** There is an additional 1d6 rolled – this feat adds +2d6 for a x2 multiplier, +3d6 for x3, and +4d6 for x4. ** Only 1d6 is rolled if [[ki damage]] is used for an attack, regardless of the critical multiplier. This results in less average damage for a critical hit (by 1 for a x2 multiplier, more for higher multipliers). So a [[weapon master]] could average more damage by not using ki damage in situations where critical hits are frequent enough (based on the [[threat range]]). * The [[creature weapon]] variant of this feat is non-functional; the [[unarmed strike]] variant is used with creature weapons (or any other [[natural weapon]]). *Weapons with the [[no combat damage]] property do not benefit from overwhelming critical.
=== Previous versions ===
* Prior to [[Enhanced Edition]] version 1.89,<!--might have been fixed earlier--> this feat did not account for a weapon master's ''[[increased multiplier]]'' feat; a [[kukri]] (normally a x2 weapon) would still get a +2d6 bonus from this feat, even when it has a x3 multiplier in the hand of a weapon master.

revision.text:
{{feat |epic=yes |type=general |prereq=21st level, [[dexterity]] 25+, <del>[[dodge]]</del>, [[tumble]] 30 [[skill rank|rank]]s, [[improved evasion]], [[defensive roll]] |desc=The character avoids the first attack each [[round]]. |use=automatic |icon=ife_x2epicdodge.gif |bonus1=rogue |bonus2=shadowdancer }}
==Notes==
*Requires [[Hordes of the Underdark]]. *The in-game description incorrectly lists ''dodge'' as a prerequisite. * The combat round is from the dodger's perspective; "first" is relative to when the dodger begins a round of combat. *This feat causes a character to automatically avoid the first ''successful'' attack or the first (possibly unsuccessful) [[attack of opportunity]] or [[riposte]] in a round, not simply the first attack in a round. ** Occasionally (when combined with [[parry]]), epic dodge may be shifted to a different successful attack in the same [[flurry]] as the first successful attack. The end result is typically the same, though. *This feat will only activate against attacks that would deal physical damage after accounting for damage [[immunity]], [[damage resistance|resistance]] and [[damage reduction|reduction]]. *Due to a bug, this feat can activate against missed ''[[ki damage]]'' attacks, missed [[called shot]]s and missed [[knockdown]] attempts. *The ''defensive roll'' and ''improved evasion'' requirements imply a [[player character|PC]] must have one of the following class level combinations in order to qualify for ''epic dodge'': ** 13 [[rogue]] levels, ** 10 [[shadowdancer]] levels, ** 10 rogue and 5 shadowdancer levels, ** 9 [[monk]] and 10 rogue levels, or ** 9 monk and 5 shadowdancer levels.
===Older versions===
*Prior to version 1.69, only a single rank in [[tumble]] was required.

{{feat |type=general |prereq=[[dexterity]] 15+ |reqfor=[[improved two-weapon fighting]] |desc=When [[dual-wield|fighting with two weapons]], this [[feat]] reduces the penalty of the [[off-hand]] weapon by 4. |use=automatic |icon=Ife_ambidex.gif |bonus1=champion of Torm |bonus2=fighter }}
==Notes== *[[Ranger]]s are prohibited from selecting this feat (on a ranger level), presumably because they receive the [[dual-wield (feat)|dual-wield]] feat at first level. (The ''dual-wield'' feat combines the effects of ''ambidexterity'' and [[two-weapon fighting]], as long as the ranger is not wearing [[medium armor|medium]] or [[heavy armor]], but does not qualify as a prerequisite for ''improved two-weapon fighting''.)
==Builder notes== '''Item feat:''' yes
No special treatment is required by this feat.
==Custom content notes== '''Removable:''' yes
'''Reusable:''' yes
'''Script:''' hardcoded
*A custom class must have this feat in their feat list, or that class will not be able to select it as a general feat.
[[category:feats restricted by class]]

revision.text: {{feat |type=class |prereq=[[bard]] |desc=Bards are able to sing a song that can bolster their allies. [[Deaf]]ened [[creature]]s are not affected by the bard's singing. The song affects all allies within 30 feet and lasts for 10 [[round]]s. The higher the bard's final [[perform]] skill and class level, the better the bard song. |use=selected |icon=ife_bardsong.gif |class1=bard }} == Notes == *This feat may be used once per [[bard]] level per day. * A ''bard song'' cannot be started while [[silence]]d, nor will it affect silenced creatures. * Depending on the power of the song, a ''bard song ''can provide bonuses to [[attack roll]]s, damage rolls, each type of [[saving throw]] (fortitude, reflex, and will), [[armor class]] (AC, specifically a [[dodge bonus]]), and [[skill]]s. It can also provide [[temporary hit point]]s (THP). **The damage bonus is listed on the character sheet as bludgeoning. However the actual damage is the type of the weapon wielded. *This feat has no effect on characters currently influenced by a bard song (excluding [[curse song]]s). A bard should be aware of this if starting a new song before an old one expires. *The feat [[lingering song]] increases the duration by 5 rounds (15 rounds total). The feat [[lasting inspiration]] increases the duration 10 times (100 rounds total). They [[stack]], but lasting inspiration is applied first; so, with both feats, the duration is 105 rounds. **Other feats that may be of interest to someone using ''bard song'' include [[extra music]] and [[curse song]]. *This ability can be used while [[polymorph]]ed. *The bonus to attack provided by this ability counts towards the +20 [[attack bonus cap]]. *The bonus to saving throws provided by this ability counts towards the +20 saving throw bonus cap. *The bonus to skills provided by this ability counts towards the +50 skill bonus cap. *The perform skill required for the highest levels of bard song is unattainable without magic items. {|class="centertable" style="text-align:center" |+Bard song bonuses |- !Bard level !Perform !! Attack !! Damage !! Will !! Fortitude !! Reflex !! THP !! AC !! Skills |- !1!!3 |1||1||0||0||0||0||0||0 |- !2!!6 |1||1||1||0||0||0||0||0 |- !3!!9 |1||2||1||1||0||0||0||0 |- style="background-color:#505050" !6!!12 |1||2||1||1||1||0||0||1 |- style="background-color:#505050" !8!!15 |2||2||1||1||1||8||0||1 |- style="background-color:#505050" !11!!18 |2||2||1||1||1||8||2||2 |- !14!!21 |2||3||1||1||1||16||3||2 |- !15!!24 |2||3||2||2||2||16||4||3 |- !16!!30 |2||3||3||2||2||20||5||4 |- style="background-color:#505050" !17!!35 |2||3||3||2||2||22||5||5 |- style="background-color:#505050" !18!!40 |2||3||3||2||2||24||5||6 |- style="background-color:#505050" !19!!45 |2||3||3||2||2||26||5||7 |- !20!!50 |2||3||3||2||2||28||5||8 |- !21!!55 |2||3||3||2||2||30||5||9 |- !22!!60 |2||3||3||2||2||32||5||11 |- style="background-color:#505050" !23!!65 |2||3||3||2||2||34||5||12 |- style="background-color:#505050" !24!!70 |2||3||3||2||2||36||5||13 |- style="background-color:#505050" !25!!75 |2||3||3||2||2||38||6||14 |- !26!!80 |2||3||3||2||2||40||6||15 |- !27!!85 |2||3||3||2||2||42||6||16 |- !28!!90 |2||3||3||2||2||44||6||17 |- style="background-color:#505050" !29!!95 |2||3||3||2||2||46||6||18 |- style="background-color:#505050" !30!!100 |2||3||3||2||2||48||7||19 |} == Builder notes == '''Item feat:''' No, but it can be added with custom content. == Custom content notes == '''Removable:''' yes '''Reusable:''' yes '''Script:''' nw_s2_bardsong, [[spells.2da]] (411), and [[feat.2da]] (257, 355-373) * This feat can be added to [[iprp_feats.2da]] to make it available as an item feat. However, since bards get this feat at level 1, there is little point in doing so unless several other changes are also made. (The [[radial menu]] option will appear only for bards unless appropriate [[cls_feat_*.2da]] files are changed. In addition, non-bards will get no benefits from the default script, as they will not meet the requirement of at least one bard level for the minimal benefits.)

revision.text:
{{feat |type=class |prereq=[[barbarian]] 2 (5, 10, 13, 16, 19); [[rogue]] 3 (6, 11, 14, 17, 20); [[shadowdancer]] 2 (5, 10); [[assassin]] 2 (5, 10) |desc=There are six versions of this feat, with cumulative (but not [[stack]]ing) benefits. (Assassins and shadowdancers only qualify for the first three versions.) The sixth version includes benefits extending into [[epic class]] levels. '''I:''' The character retains his [[dexterity]] bonus to [[armor class|AC]], even if caught [[flat-foot]]ed or attacked by a hidden or [[invisible]] creature. '''II:''' This feat grants a +1 bonus on [[reflex]] [[saving throw]]s made to avoid [[trap]]s. '''III:''' This feat grants a +2 bonus on reflex saving throws made to avoid traps. '''IV:''' This feat grants a +3 bonus on reflex saving throws made to avoid traps. '''V:''' This feat grants a +4 bonus on reflex saving throws made to avoid traps. '''VI+:''' This feat grants a +5 bonus on reflex saving throws made to avoid traps.
Epic progression: The ''uncanny dodge'' bonus improves by +1 every three [[class level|level]]s. |use=automatic |icon=ife_uncdodge.gif |class1=assassin |class2=barbarian |class3=rogue |class4=shadowdancer }}__NOTOC__ == Notes == * Contrary to its name, uncanny dodge does not allow a character to retain [[dodge bonus]]es to AC when flat-footed, only the dexterity bonus. * Uncanny dodge can be extremely helpful for dexterity-based builds in avoiding attacks from hidden creatures, as it allows retention of what could be a significant portion of their AC. * The bonus to reflex saves versus traps is subject to the +20 [[saving throw]] cap. * As of [[Enhanced Edition]] patch 1.74, ''uncanny dodge II'' grants immunity to sneak attacks from a [[flank]]ing attacker unless the attacker has at least four more combined [[class level]]s of rogue, assassin, barbarian, and shadowdancer than the defender. ([[blackguard]] levels are not counted.) For example, a level 10 rogue would have this immunity when attacked by a level 13 rogue, but not when attacked by a level 14 rogue. This immunity does not apply when the defender is [[flat-foot]]ed. This change is undocumented in the feat description. The pre-Enhanced Edition behavior can be restored by setting FLANK_LEVEL_RANGE in [[Ruleset.2da]] to -99. '''See also:''' [[Defensive awareness]] ==Builder notes== '''Item feat:''' No, but it can be added with custom content. ==Custom content notes== '''Removable:''' yes '''Reusable:''' yes '''Script:''' hardcoded *These feats can be added to [[iprp_feats.2da]] to make them available as item feats. *''Uncanny dodge I'' is required to preserve dexterity AC when flat-footed. * Each version of ''uncanny dodge'' will grant its reflex bonus without the need for lower feat(s).

{{feat |epic=yes |type=general |prereq=21st level, [[wisdom]] 30+, either [[wild shape]] 6x/day or [[greater wildshape IV]] |desc=The character may use wild shape to [[polymorph|change into]] a [[dragon]]. The transformation has a duration of 1 [[hour]] per [[class level]]. |use=selected. After selecting, the character must choose what type of dragon they will appear as. |icon=ife_x2wshpdrag.gif |bonus1=druid |bonus2=shifter }}__NOTOC__ == Dragon forms == Dragon shapes are [[size modifier|huge]] [[polymorph]]s that merge [[item property|properties]] from the [[item]]s in the [[armor slot]], [[helmet slot]], and (if it's a [[shield]]) the [[off-hand slot]]. (Unlike [[greater wildshape I|wyrmling shapes]], miscellaneous items are not merged.) Whether or not the merged properties [[stack]] depends on whether or not those properties would stack when placed on the same item. Typically, this means that only [[regeneration]] will stack. As with many polymorphs, dragon shapes override the character's [[strength]], [[dexterity]], and [[constitution]], as well as provide [[temporary hit point]]s, a new [[armor class]], and [[natural weapon]]s. The following stats are shared by all available dragon types. {| class="centertable" |- ! Str !! Dex !! Con !! THP !! AC !! Attack
modifier !! Damage |- |48||36||32|| +100||41|| claw: +23
bite: +17||claw: 2d8+25
bite: 2d8+19 |} In addition, dragon shapes have [[spell resistance]] 20, [[true seeing]], [[damage reduction]] 40/+6, and immunity to [[mind-affecting|mind spells]], [[sneak attack]], and [[paralysis]]. The armor class comes from the standard base (10), plus the [[ability modifier|dexterity modifier]] (13), a [[dodge bonus]] included in the polymorph (20), and the [[size modifier]] (-2). This will be further modified by the highest bonus from the merged items. The type of the bonus does not matter, as all item bonuses are converted to [[deflection bonus|deflection]] as part of the polymorph. In addition, other modifiers from non-item sources still apply (these are not converted to deflection by the polymorph). The natural weapons consist of two [[claw item|claws]] and one [[bite item|bite]]; the game randomly chooses one of these weapons for each attack. The listed attack modifier for the claws includes the strength modifier (19), an [[enhancement bonus]] (6), and the size modifier (-2). The bite is similar, but lacks the enhancement bonus. This modifier is added to [[attack bonus|the other normal modifiers to attack rolls]]; in the simplest case, these other modifiers consist of just the character's [[base attack bonus]]. Natural weapons come with some caveats that are applicable to dragon shapes. First, the dragon's natural weapons will be able to bypass X/+6 damage reduction thanks to the dragon's own X/+6 damage reduction, even though the bite lacks an enhancement bonus. Second, natural weapons interact inconsistently with weapon-specific feats. Notably, [[improved critical]] (unarmed strike) and [[overwhelming critical]] (unarmed strike) work while using natural weapons. However, [[weapon focus]] (unarmed strike), [[epic weapon focus]] (unarmed strike) and [[devastating critical]] (unarmed strike) do not work. There are three types of dragon available through this feat. Aside from cosmetic differences, these types differ in their breath weapon, damage [[immunity]], and damage [[vulnerability]]. The breath weapon of a dragon without at least 10 [[class level|levels]] of shifter suffers a -4 penalty on the DC and has the number of damage dice reduced by 4. {| class="centertable" |- ! Dragon !! Breath !! Immunity !! Vulnerability |- class="BlueDragon" |[[ancient blue dragon form|Blue, ancient]] || [[lightning dragon breath (shifter)|lightning]] || [[electrical damage|electrical]] 100% ||  |- class="GreenDragon" |[[ancient green dragon form|Green, ancient]] || [[gas dragon breath (shifter)|gas]] || [[acid damage|acid]] 100% ||  |- class="RedDragon" |[[ancient red dragon form|Red, ancient]] || [[fire dragon breath (shifter)|fire]] || [[fire damage|fire]] 100% || [[cold damage|cold]] 50% |} == Notes == * Requires [[Hordes of the Underdark]]. * This feat can only be acquired when advancing in [[druid]] or [[shifter]] levels. * Despite the description the duration is permanent. * This is the only epic shape feat that is available to druids without shifter levels. * This form of shapeshifting cannot be dispelled. * Unlike normal dragon monsters, a character will not gain a fear-aura when shapeshifted to a dragon. * Due to the high wisdom requirement of this feat, a single [[monk]] level — with its associated wisdom-based [[monk AC bonus]] — can greatly benefit a character with dragon shape. Furthermore, the monk level provides the monk's [[unarmed base attack bonus|unarmed attack progression]], [[stunning fist]] (with a decent DC), and [[discipline]] and [[tumble]] as [[class skill]]s. Moreover, a character can equip a shield before assuming dragon form, which will cause the shield's properties to be merged but will not — while shifted — disable those monk bonuses that are normally disabled when a shield is equipped. * A common way to quickly meet the wisdom requirement of this feat is taking levels of [[champion of Torm]] after level 20; this class gets a bonus feat every two levels (up to class level 10), and [[great wisdom]] is one of the choices (for epic characters). * This feat can only be used three times a day (despite the description stating that the character is "using wild shape" to turn into a dragon). * Because of the dragon's huge size, he may not fit through small doors or corridors, etc. Thus, one must use the limited daily uses wisely. === Previous versions === * Prior to version 1.69, this feat only required wild shape 5x/day, not 6x/day as stated in the in-game description. * When the Hordes of the Underdark was originally released, this creature had only meager damage reduction (5/+1), and its claws only did 2d6 damage, lacking the +6 enhancement. == Custom content notes == *A custom class must have this feat in their feat list, or that class will not be able to select it as a [[general feat]]. *''script:'' X2_S2_GWildShp *''breath attack script:'' X2_S2_EDragBrth [[category:feats restricted by class, epic]]
